import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_1.csv"
    
    # Define target output path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    
    # Load Source 0: user ratings data
    # Schema: ['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
    df_ratings = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    
    # Load Source 1: movie metadata
    # Schema includes ['item_id', 'movie title', ...]
    df_movies = pd.read_csv(source1_path)
    
    # We only need 'item_id' and 'movie title' from Source 1 for the join
    df_movies_reduced = df_movies[['item_id', 'movie title']]
    
    # Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'item_id' to get movie titles for each rating
    df_merged = pd.merge(df_ratings, df_movies_reduced, on='item_id', how='left')
    
    # Ensure the target schema and types:
    # ['user_id': int, 'item_id': int, 'rating': int, 'timestamp': int, 'movie title': str]
    df_merged = df_merged.astype({
        'user_id': 'int64',
        'item_id': 'int64',
        'rating': 'int64',
        'timestamp': 'int64',
        'movie title': 'string'
    })
    
    # Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
    df_target = df_merged[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]
    
    # Write the transformed data to the target CSV file without the index
    df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
    
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
